close_reason: Fixed in commit 247fb69 alongside .72. Pins the regression from bd:JMAP-g7wu.2.4.9 in the doc surface. Test at integration.rs:3729-3733 verifies the impl-side contract; the rustdoc now mirrors it.
description:
## Finding

`ChatBackend::apply_space_patch`'s rustdoc
(`crate-jmap-chat-server/src/backend.rs:441-509`) is silent on the
cross-type state-token-bump requirement for ops that mutate `Chat`
records as a side effect.

The kit's integration tests assert that AddCategory /
UpdateCategory ops carrying a `channelIds` array — which mutates
`Chat.categoryId` for each named channel — MUST emit
`Chat/changes` entries for every relocated channel.

## Test

`crate-jmap-chat-server/tests/integration.rs:3729-3733`:

```rust
assert_eq!(
    updated,
    vec!["ch-p", "ch-q"],
    "Chat/changes must list both cascaded channels as updated: {updated:?}"
);
```

Regression-context comment at `integration.rs:3677-3680`
verbatim:

> before that bead, the `set_channel_category` cascade silently
> mutated Chat records without producing a `Chat/changes` entry,
> leaving subscribers unaware of the categoryId change.

This describes a previously-fixed real bug (the cascade omitted
the state bump). The fix landed but the contract that prevents
its recurrence is encoded only in the test, not the rustdoc.

## What goes wrong for a third-party implementer

A third-party backend that implements AddCategory /
UpdateCategory by:

1. Writing to the `Category` aggregate / `Space.categories`
   collection, AND
2. Updating `Chat.categoryId` on each affected channel,

but FORGETS to bump the `Chat` type's state token, silently
breaks every Chat/changes subscriber. Clients see chats sitting
in their previous category indefinitely, even after a fresh
`Chat/get` returns the new `categoryId`. The bug is silent until
a user noticed their categorization changes don't propagate.

## Why this is a separate finding from the RemoveChannel cascade

The sibling finding (RemoveChannel destroys Messages + bumps
Message state) covers the **destructive** cascade. This one
covers the **mutating-cross-type** cascade: a Space-level op
mutates `Chat` records without destroying them, and the state
bump is the only signal subscribers get.

Both are members of a broader workspace cross-type-state-bump
convention that the rustdoc captures nowhere. They share the
recommended fix (one new "Cross-type cascade contract" rustdoc
section) but the failure modes and the test fixtures are
distinct enough to file separately.

## Recommendation

In the same "Cross-type cascade contract" rustdoc section
proposed by the RemoveChannel cascade finding, add:

> ### Side-effect mutations on Chat
>
> Ops that mutate `Chat.categoryId` as a side effect of
> Space-level changes (e.g. `AddCategory` / `UpdateCategory`
> with a non-empty `channelIds` array, `RemoveCategory` that
> falls channels back to no-category) MUST bump the `Chat`
> type's state token for each affected channel.
> `Chat/changes` subscribers rely on this bump to see the
> `categoryId` change; without it, their local cache of channel
> categorization drifts silently from server reality.
>
> Similarly for `Member` / `Role` / `ReadPosition` records
> mutated as side effects of Space-level ops: the touched
> records' type state tokens MUST be bumped.

## Engineering basis

- Test assertion at `integration.rs:3729-3733` verbatim.
- Regression-context comment at `integration.rs:3677-3680`
  verbatim — explicitly identifies "before that bead" the
  silent-mutation bug existed in the reference impl.
- Rustdoc at `backend.rs:441-509` read end-to-end; no
  cross-type-state-bump language present.

## Priority justification

P1, same justification as the RemoveChannel cascade finding:
silent failure, multi-client correctness gap, doc-only fix,
high leverage. The fact that this bug HAS BEEN historically
present in the kit's own reference impl (per the comment at
`integration.rs:3677-3680`) is direct evidence that the
contract is non-obvious and the doc gap matters in practice.
title: API contract: apply_space_patch category-add-with-channelIds MUST bump Chat/changes for relocated channels; rustdoc silent
